marco: Heads-up — saw a ~12% p50/p95 token latency regression when streaming lots of very short responses (<= 8 tokens) on rtx-pool this morning.

alisha: repro? which model and kernel? :eyes:

marco: repro on open-7b-quant, kernel-selector chose small-kernel (fast single-token path) but we keep preempting for partial-decode flushes, so we end up bouncing between kernels. repro gist: small concurrent stream load, many 1-6 token responses.

ryan: hmm that sounds like a decision boundary issue in kernel selection + batching. selector currently uses `seq_len_est` and `seen_prefix_ratio`. If partial-decode preempts, effective seq distribution shifts.

tara: can you paste the perf samples? even a tiny snippet helps.

marco: pasted profiling sample from devbox:
```
# perf top-snapshot (shortened)
stream_handler.handle_request                 42%
kernel_dispatch(small)                       28%
kernel_dispatch(large)                       5%
kv_cache_lookup                               8%
partial_decode_manager                       12%
context-switch / scheduling                   5%
```
observed: lots of time in handler juggling partial-decode timers.

alisha: ok. two levers to try: 1) bump token-budget floor for mini-batches so we don't form too many tiny batches, 2) add a cheap pre-decode check to avoid switching kernels mid-stream.

ryan: agree. also kernel selector could use a transient flag `streaming_inflight` that biases toward the medium kernel when partial-decode rate > 10%. prevents thrash.

marco: tried quick experiment locally: set token_budget = {min:32, target:96, max:512} and added `prefer_stable_kernel` on streaming requests. p50 improved ~7% and p95 improved ~9% for our load.

tara: nice. any KV cache changes? we saw a bunch of cold lookups earlier.

marco: KV behaved weird: small-kernel path was not reusing warmed KV pages because of different packing; caused duplicate warm-ups. increased overall latency when combined with preemptions.

alisha: that suggests we need a canonical KV layout override for streaming paths so both kernels can reuse same strides. low-effort: unify key packing for prefix-only accesses.

ryan: also add metric `stream_partial_preempts` (counter + windowed rate). then we can trigger `prefer_stable_kernel` automatically when rate exceeds threshold.

perf-bot: automated benchmark run queued: run/stream-mini-batch-2026-03-18-1 (ETA ~15m). :robot_face:

marco: for scheduling partial-decode, my notes:
- if request is flagged `stream:true` and `expected_tokens <= 8`, prefer early-send but hold if batch token_budget < min to avoid micro-batches.
- allow one extra slot for in-flight partial-decode so we don't preempt kernel selection.

tara: can you sketch the pseudo-rule? i'll implement in scheduler.

marco: pseudo: `if streaming and expected_tokens<=small_thresh and batch_tokens >= token_budget.min then send_early else coalesce_until_target`

ryan: minor tweak: compute `expected_tokens` as `max(user_hint, max_historical_run, median_recent)` to avoid noisy single-sample hints.

alisha: action items: 1) tara - implement token_budget tunable + scheduler rule (PR), 2) ryan - add `stream_partial_preempts` metric and kernel bias flag autopolicy, 3) marco - follow-up on KV packing patch and run canary.

tara: i'll open PRs today. will add tests for micro-batch scenarios and a simple sim harness to validate no extra re-compiles.

marco: thanks. if the perf-bot run confirms, we can flip the default for streaming-heavy projects.

ryan: also add a small dashboard: streaming throughput, partial_preempt_rate, kernel_switch_count, kv_warm_hits. helps correlate regressions.

alisha: agreed. set rollback knob to `prefer_stable_kernel=false` behind a feature flag.

marco: awesome — will monitor. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: run/stream-mini-batch-2026-03-18-1 completed: p50 -7.2%, p95 -8.8% for the test workload (details in benchmark link).

tara: perfect, merging the token_budget PR now.

marco: will follow with KV packing patch and a short replay harness to ensure no regression for long-seq workloads.

alisha: great coordination — thanks everyone.
